sources.entry: Music Assistant | Music library manager and player for smart speakers

summary.one_liner: Music Assistant Server is an open-source media library manager that connects to streaming services and networked speakers, designed to run on an always-on device alongside Home Assistant.
summary.what_it_does: The server acts as the core of Music Assistant, a media library manager that connects to streaming services and a range of connected speakers. The README says it is built to run side by side with Home Assistant and is meant for automation, with the recommended setup being a Home Assistant app. A Docker container image (ghcr.io/music-assistant/server) is the other officially supported method. The README states that the server bundles its system dependencies such as ffmpeg 7.0+, jemalloc and CIFS/NFS client libraries, and it is not published to PyPI. For development, it can run from source with Python 3.14+ and ffmpeg 7.0+, using a setup script, a local run command, pytest and pre-commit linters. Documentation and an issue tracker are linked from the README.
use_cases: Play music from streaming services on smart speakers
Manage a local music library on an always-on device
Automate music playback with Home Assistant
Run a music server on a Raspberry Pi or NAS
Control speakers from one media library
how_to_run: Recommended: install as a Home Assistant app (see project documentation)
Development: scripts/setup.sh to create the virtualenv and install dependencies
Development: python -m music_assistant --log-level debug to run the server locally
Development: pre-commit run --all-files to run linters
notable: Designed to run as a Home Assistant app, with automation as the main goal
Bundles system dependencies so it does not need a plain pip install
Not published to PyPI; official builds are the Home Assistant app and the Docker image
Runs on always-on hardware such as a Raspberry Pi, NAS or Intel NUC
caveats: Third-party packages such as Linux distribution builds are not supported, and their issues may be closed
Bundled service credentials are licensed only for official builds, so other builds must supply their own
Requires an always-on device and a recent ffmpeg (7.0+) with a specific codec set for source installs
